explanation: The hinge of the whole narrative: strategic commodities and strategic ground exchanged for industrial capital. Wikipedia states the sequence — in 1942, following the American proposal to finance the CSN, United States forces established air bases along Brazil’s north-eastern coast — and states the bargain: in exchange for raw materials the United States provided equipment, technical assistance and financing for a Brazilian steel mill, settled in July 1940. Roosevelt’s Good Neighbor policy is where the financing sat, and reports at the time said the United States had a plan to invade the Northeast if Vargas insisted on neutrality. What Brazil bought with the Atlantic narrows was the plant at Volta Redonda.
